newsitem.title: TURKEY: Fugitive Nadir vows return to Turkey investments.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive Nadir vows return to Turkey investments.

text.p: Fugitive Turkish Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir vowed on Thursday to return to his investments in Turkey, four years after jumping bail in Britain, state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
"I will return to my investments in Turkey," Nadir told the agency after making the opening address on Cyprus FM, a new radio station he has established in the breakaway northern Cypriot state.
Anatolian said it was not clear when he planned to return to his business interests in Turkey, where in the past he invested in electronics companies, a hotel and the media.
Nadir fled in May 1993 while awaiting trial on theft and false accounting charges following the collapse of his London-based Polly Peck fruits-to-electronics empire.
He still has media, banking and tourism interests in northern Cyprus.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 after a short-lived military coup on the island. Only Ankara recognises the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.
